examples.en: The newborn next door cries all night.

examples.ko: 갓난아이를 안을 때는 목을 받쳐 주세요.
examples.en: When you hold a newborn, support its neck.
Traveling with a newborn is not easy.
He fell fast asleep like a newborn baby.
They say breast milk is best for a newborn.

examples.ko: 우리 조카는 아직 갓난아이라서 하루 종일 자요.
examples.en: My nephew is still a newborn, so he sleeps all day.

explain: 태어난 지 얼마 안 된 아기를 말해요. 일상에서는 그냥 '아기'를 가장 많이 쓰고, '신생아'는 병원이나 뉴스처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요. '갓난애'는 줄여서 편하게 말할 때 나와요.

phrases.nuance_ko: '갓난아이'를 줄인 말이라 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 갓난아이 for casual talk.

phrases.en: I saw a newborn at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 뉴스처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in formal settings like hospitals and the news.

phrases.en: My aunt takes care of a newborn baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기를 보살피는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for looking after a baby.
phrases.en_equiv: to take care of a newborn

explain_en: It refers to a baby who was born very recently. In daily life '아기' is most common, and '신생아' is used in formal settings such as hospitals or news. '갓난애' is the shortened, more casual form.

examples.en: A thief broke into our house last night.

examples.ko: 경찰이 그 사람을 도둑놈으로 의심하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police suspect that man of being a thief.

examples.ko: 비싸게 팔다니, 가게 주인이 도둑놈 같아요.
examples.en: Selling it at that price, the shop owner is like a thief.
I had my wallet stolen by a thief at the market.

examples.ko: 영화에서 도둑놈과 경찰이 계속 서로 쫓고 쫓겨요.
examples.en: In the movie, the thief and the police keep chasing each other.
I heard the thieves broke the shop door and went in.

explain: '도둑'보다 거칠고, 화가 났거나 아주 친한 사이에서 쓰는 말이에요. 뉴스나 공식적인 자리에서는 '도둑'이나 '범인'이라고 해요. '놈'은 사람을 낮춰 부르는 말이라서 윗사람 앞에서는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 것을 거저 얻으려는 욕심 많은 마음을 비난할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize a greedy wish to get something for nothing.

explain_en: This is rougher than '도둑' and is used when you are angry or with close friends. In news or formal settings people say '도둑' or '범인'. '놈' is a word that looks down on a person, so do not use it in front of elders.

examples.en: The creditors came every day and knocked on the door.
He kept moving to avoid his creditors.

examples.ko: 빚쟁이한테 쫓기는 주인공이 나오는 드라마를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a drama with a main character chased by debt collectors.

examples.ko: 빚쟁이의 독촉이 대단해서 안 갚을 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: The creditor's demands were so intense that I couldn't help but repay.

examples.ko: 빚쟁이에게 시달리다 보니 잠도 못 잤어요.
examples.en: Being hounded by creditors, I couldn't even sleep.

examples.ko: 옛날 이야기에는 빚쟁이가 집까지 찾아오는 장면이 많아요.
examples.en: Old stories have many scenes where a creditor comes right to the house.

explain: 주로 돈을 받으려고 찾아오는 사람을 가리키는 말로 드라마나 이야기에 많이 나와요. 빚진 사람을 가리키기도 하고, 격식 있게는 '채권자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I paid back all the money I borrowed to the creditor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빚쟁이'보다 격식 있는 말이라 법이나 뉴스, 서류에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal word than 빚쟁이, used in law, news, and documents.

phrases.en: He was chased by his creditors and kept running away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빚을 갚지 못해 돈 받으려는 사람을 피해 다니는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone cannot repay a debt and is avoiding the people who want the money.

phrases.en: Every night a creditor came to the house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 받으러 직접 오는 장면에서 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said in scenes where someone comes in person to collect money.

explain_en: It mostly refers to a person who comes to collect money and appears often in dramas and stories. It can also refer to the person who owes the debt, and the formal word for a creditor is '채권자'.

en: to spread rumors; to gossip; to tell rumors

examples.en: Please don't spread this story to anyone.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 내 비밀을 온 동네에 소문냈어요.
examples.en: That person spread my secret all over the neighborhood.
Please spread the word to your friends that the shop is open.
It's a good restaurant, so I want to tell everyone about it.
It would be a problem if you spread this around.
I didn't mean to spread it around on purpose.

explain: 소문을 일부러 퍼뜨릴 때 써요. 나쁜 소문뿐 아니라 좋은 가게나 기쁜 소식을 널리 알릴 때도 쓸 수 있어요. 스스로 퍼지는 것은 '소문나다'(소문이 나다)를 써요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 남의 얘기를 여기저기 소문내고 다녀요.
phrases.en: That person goes around spreading other people's stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 다니다'를 붙이면 여러 곳에 계속 퍼뜨리는 모습이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 다니다' shows someone keeps spreading it around in many places.

phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 말투라서 '소문내지 마세요'보다 더 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request form that sounds softer than '소문내지 마세요'.

phrases.en: I told my friends all about the new shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 쓰는 반말이고, 좋은 소식을 알릴 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for close friends; it can also be used for spreading good news.

explain_en: It is used when someone deliberately spreads a rumor. It can be about bad gossip, but also about a good shop or happy news. When it spreads by itself, use '소문나다' (소문이 나다).

examples.ko: 다음 달에 가족들만 모여서 약혼식을 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to hold an engagement ceremony next month with just family.
Both sets of parents came to the engagement ceremony.
I had a hanbok made to wear on the engagement day.

examples.ko: 약혼식이 끝나고 다 같이 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: After the engagement ceremony, we all took a photo together.

examples.ko: 약혼식 없이 바로 결혼하는 커플도 있어요.
examples.en: Some couples marry right away without an engagement ceremony.

examples.ko: 약혼식에서 받은 반지를 아직도 끼고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm still wearing the ring I received at the engagement ceremony.

explain: '약혼'은 결혼을 약속하는 일이고, '약혼식'은 그것을 알리는 행사예요. 약혼식을 따로 하지 않고 양가 부모님이 처음 만나는 '상견례'만 하는 경우도 있어요.

phrases.en: We held an engagement ceremony at a small restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 연다고 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase for holding the event.

phrases.en: I attended my friend's engagement ceremony.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you go as a guest.

phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 아니라 결혼을 약속하는 일 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the promise to marry itself, not the event.

explain_en: '약혼' is promising to marry, and '약혼식' is the event that marks it. Some couples skip a separate engagement ceremony and only hold a '상견례', the first meeting between the two families.
